name: South Ridge (via Asa Peak NE Ridge)

pitch_detail.notes: South ridge crest, several pitches, climbing on or left of the crest; rope up starting south of Point 7760.
Where the crest becomes too craggy, downclimb one pitch to a ledge system and traverse north to a whaleback formation.
From the 7,480-ft south col, traverse a high snowpatch then ascend a broad ramp just left of a snow-filled gully, dog-legging right to the headwall.
Crux chimney on the summit headwall.
One additional roped pitch above the chimney.
Final ~100 ft of scrambling to the true summit.

rappel_detail.notes: First of three rappels down the chimney and headwall band.
rappel_detail.anchor: not described; carry cord to build or back up
rappel_detail.station: Above the 5.8 chimney and headwall, after downclimbing the final scramble and reversing the roped pitch above the chimney.
Within the chimney and headwall band, at the end of the first rappel.

rappel_detail.notes: Third rappel, into the upper gully. Then descend the east-facing snow couloir about 1,400 vertical feet, with flukes and running belays, to the south col.
rappel_detail.station: The lowest station in the chimney and headwall band.

rappels: 3 rappels through the headwall/chimney band to reach the upper gully, then an ~1,400-ft descending traverse of an east-facing snow couloir back to the south col
descent_text: From the summit, downclimb the last ~100 ft of Class 2-3 terrain, then reverse the roped pitch above the chimney and rappel the 5.8 chimney/headwall (3 rappels total) to regain the upper gully. From there, descend an east-facing snow couloir for roughly 1,400 vertical feet using snow flukes and running belays back to the south col at ~7,480 ft, then reverse the traverse and ridge pitches back toward Icy-Spruce Pass camp — a round trip reported at roughly 19-20 hours from high camp on one ascent.
approach: From High Bridge in Stehekin, follow the PCT/Agnes Creek Trail south roughly 8-10 miles (about 5.2 hours to a Swamp Creek-area camp) to the Agnes Creek/Spruce Creek confluence. Cross Agnes Creek on a log, then Spruce Creek on another log shortly after, and climb steeply northwest off-trail through brush, talus, and slabs to a camp near Upper Blue Basin (~5,000 ft), then continue to a high camp near Icy-Spruce Pass (~6,760 ft) for the summit push.
overview: The standard/recommended line on Agnes: gain the south ridge via a high traverse from Icy-Spruce Pass and the Northeast Ridge of Asa Peak, then climb a mix of 4th/low-5th-class ridge pitches and a 5.8 chimney crux on the summit headwall to the top. The peak's first ascent, in 1936, came up from the West Fork of Agnes Creek rather than by this ridge; the second ascent did not follow until 1969, and only fourteen parties had reached the summit by 1987.
beta: Described as the recommended route: gain Asa Peak's Northeast Ridge, traverse to Agnes's south ridge, and climb short technical sections up to 5.6-5.8. From a high camp near Icy-Spruce Pass, parties make a rising traverse over snow, talus, and slabs to the south ridge crest south of Point 7760, then rope up for several pitches of Class 4-5 rock on or left of the crest. Where the crest gets too craggy, downclimb one pitch to a ledge system and traverse to a whaleback with views of the summit block. From the 7,480-ft south col, traverse a high snowpatch and ascend a broad Class 2-3 ramp just left of a snow-filled gully, dog-legging right to a headwall; a 5.8 chimney (the crux) and one more roped pitch lead to a final ~100-ft Class 2-3 scramble to the summit.
face: South Ridge, reached via the Northeast Ridge of neighboring Asa Peak; upper headwall faces roughly NW
